approved: Clean Energy Legislation (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013 [No. 2]
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax and includes measures to prevent price exploitation after the repeal.

The bill would prohibit businesses from engaging in carbon-specific price exploitation for key goods like electricity and gas, and ban false or misleading representations about the carbon tax repeal's effect on prices.
The maximum penalty for a corporation that breaches the price exploitation prohibition would be 6,471 penalty units ($1,100,070), and for an individual, 1,295 penalty units ($220,150).
Introduces a new prohibition on carbon-specific price exploitation for key goods.
Gives the ACCC monitoring powers to assess the effect of the carbon tax repeal on prices.
Prohibits false or misleading representations about the carbon tax repeal's effect on prices.
Businesses that supply key goods such as electricity and gas, and consumers who purchase those goods.

This division relates to the Policy _[For a carbon price](/policies/3)_. The majority voted against [amendments](http://www.openaustralia.org/debates/?id=2014-06-26.119.2) introduced by Labor MP [Mark Butler](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/mp.php?mpn=Mark_Butler&mpc=Port_Adelaide&house=representatives).(Read the amendments and the Government's response to them [here](http://www.openaustralia.org/debates/?id=2014-06-26.119.2). ) This means that they have been rejected. The amendments related to keeping an emissions trading scheme. _Background to the bills_ The [Clean Energy Legislation (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013 (No. 2)](http://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r5292) was introduced with a number of other related bills to remove the [carbon pricing mechanism](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_pricing_in_Australia), which was introduced by the Australian Labor Party while in government. The Coalition described the mechanism as a “carbon tax” and removing it was a key policy platform during the 2013 election.(You can read more about the Coalition's policy to remove the carbon price [here](http://www.liberal.org.au/scrapping-carbon-tax-and-reducing-cost-living). ) The carbon pricing mechanism commenced on 1 July 2012.(For more information on the carbon pricing mechanism and how it works, please see the Clean Energy Regulator’s [website](http://www.cleanenergyregulator.gov.au/Carbon-Pricing-Mechanism/About-the-Mechanism/Pages/default.aspx). ) It is an emissions trading scheme that puts a price on carbon emissions. It applies to “liable entities” (a group that includes companies that emit a high level of greenhouse gases). Initially the price of carbon is fixed by the mechanism but from 1 July 2015 the price will be set by the market, though the Labor Government did announce plans to bring this forward to 1 July 2014 just before they were defeated by the Coalition in the 2013 election. Opposed the carbon tax repeal, citing that renewable energy produced over 14 per cent of Australia's power in 2013 and more than two million households had installed clean energy systems, and cited modelling finding the renewable energy target would save households more than $500 million on power bills by 2020.

Argued in support of an amendment to establish an emissions trading scheme, citing Pacific leaders' criticism of Australia's climate stance, a fall of seven per cent in electricity market emissions under the carbon price, and said ninety-eight per cent of economists believe the government's Direct Action policy will not work.
Moved to vary the House's 24 June resolution on the carbon tax repeal package so that the Clean Energy Finance Corporation Abolition Bill would be excluded and considered instead at the next sitting.
